hits.title: SEG Solar 4 GW Tomball Texas Facility Opens as Company Eyes Nation's Largest Module Maker Status
hits.snippet: The SEG Solar Tomball Texas facility officially opened on August 7, 2026, marking a 4 GW solar module assembly plant that pushes the company toward becoming the largest crystalline silicon module manufacturer in the United States. Located in Tomball, just outside Houston, the plant joins SEG’s original 2 GW facility to lift the company’s annual domestic module assembly capacity to roughly 6 GW once fully operational next year. SEG Solar, founded in 2021 and led by CEO Jim Wood and founder and COO Jun Zhuge, represents an investment exceeding $200 million and spans nearly 500,000 square feet, or about 46,400 square metres, of manufacturing space. The Tomball opening was delivered through a straightforward corporate build out rather than a traditional public procurement process, with SEG financing and constructing the plant itself as part of a broader localization strategy. At the ceremony, SEG also unveiled plans for a second Tomball facility, a further 4.6 GW expansion to be built within 18 months directly across the street, which would push the company’s total annual capacity to 10.6 GW and make it the largest crystalline silicon module assembler in the country. hits.title: SEG Solar Inaugurates 4-GW HJT Panel Facility in Tomball, Texas - News and Statistics - IndexBox
hits.snippet: SEG Solar has officially opened its second U.S. module assembly plant, a 4-GW-per-year operation located in Tomball, Texas. SEG Solar's new Tomball facility boosts U.S. solar manufacturing with 4 GW HJT capacity, supporting AI-driven energy demand. The company already runs a 2-GW module facility in nearby Houston and is currently developing a third plant in the same region. The Tomball facility, backed by a $200 million investment and covering over 500,000 square feet, ranks among the largest heterojunction technology (HJT) module production sites in the nation. It houses four advanced manufacturing lines focused on producing SEG's newest high-efficiency SIERRA N series HJT modules, compatible with both 210-mm and 210R wafer sizes. While work proceeds on the third module factory, SEG has revealed plans to evaluate a silicon cell production facility, aiming to strengthen its domestic supply chain integration. hits.snippet: # SEG Solar Announces New US 4 GW Solar Module Factory HOUSTON – May 7, 2026 – SEG Solar (“SEG”), a leading U.S. solar module manufacturer, today announced that it will establish a new 4-gigawatt (GW) solar manufacturing facility in Houston, Texas. Building on the success of its first 2 GW solar module factory, this expansion will increase SEG’s total annual U.S. module production capacity to approximately 6 GW. Commercial operations at the new facility are expected to commence in Q3 2026. The new facility includes nearly 500,000 square feet and represents an investment of over $200 million and the creation of up to 800 new jobs. This expansion is part of SEG’s long-term localization strategy and will result in SEG becoming one of the largest 100% U.S.-owned module manufacturers. The domestically-produced modules will provide greater product quality, traceability and delivery speed to increase value for partners and customers. “This new facility marks an important milestone for SEG,” said Timothy Johnson, VP of Operations of SEG Solar. “It will further strengthen our U.S. manufacturing capabilities while supporting ongoing technology innovation.
